title: GMAO SaaS
description: Backend-first SaaS application for industrial maintenance management (GMAO), currently under active development. Multi-tenant architecture with per-tenant data isolation, permission-based access control, and a membership and invitation model. Built with FastAPI, asynchronous SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, and Alembic migrations.
caseStudy:
A backend-first SaaS application for industrial maintenance management (GMAO), currently under active development. The project is an exercise in backend architecture rather than a shipped product: multi-tenant data modelling, authentication and authorisation, and API design.

The tenant model is the architectural core. Each tenant represents an independent organisation with its own users, permissions, and domain data. Tenant isolation is a first-class requirement, not an afterthought layered on later — the data model and the query layer both reflect it. Membership is managed through an invitation flow rather than open registration, so tenant creation remains controlled.

Authentication and authorisation are separated. Authentication issues sessions; authorisation is permission-based rather than role-based. A user can hold different roles across different tenants, and access checks resolve through the membership chain rather than against a flat role on the user.

Persistence uses **FastAPI** with **asynchronous SQLAlchemy** on **PostgreSQL**, with **Alembic** migrations. Development infrastructure is containerised with **Docker** and **Docker Compose**.

**Implemented:** tenant model and isolation, authentication, authorisation, permission-based access control, tenant membership and invitation workflows, core domain model with migrations.

**Planned and in progress:** asynchronous background processing for scheduled maintenance tasks, reporting on maintenance history, additional domain modules.

**Role:** Backend Engineer — architecture and implementation.
**Status:** Private — active development. Not deployed, no public repository.
**Focus:** Multi-tenant architecture, authentication, authorisation, permission models, API and database design.

title: yb-observability
description: Open-source Python library for reusable application configuration and logging infrastructure, published on PyPI.
caseStudy:
An open-source Python library providing reusable configuration and logging infrastructure for Python applications.

The configuration loader supports YAML files with environment variable resolution, validation, and safe handling of values that contain characters which would otherwise break the YAML structure (colons, hashes, newlines). This is a small but genuinely useful safety property: the substitution runs after parsing rather than before, so a value like `NAME="foo: bar"` cannot corrupt the document. Logging is built on Loguru with consistent formatting, per-service log directories, and daily rotation with retention.

Published and available on PyPI, making it directly installable and reusable across Python projects.

```bash
pip install yb-observability
```

**Role:** Python / Backend Engineer.
**Status:** Public — published on PyPI, tested, with CI (Ruff, Pyright, Pytest).
**Focus:** Configuration and logging infrastructure, injection-safe substitution, tested public API.

title: ft_transcendence
description: A real-time multiplayer Pong and chat platform built as the final 1337 Common Core project, combining a React frontend, NestJS backend, PostgreSQL, Docker, and WebSockets.
caseStudy:
The final project of the 1337 Common Core: a full-stack multiplayer platform combining online Pong with a Discord-style chat experience.

The system uses a **NestJS** backend, **React** frontend, **PostgreSQL**, Docker Compose, JWT authentication, and Socket.IO for real-time communication. The architecture separates the frontend and backend while maintaining synchronized game and communication state.

```text
React / Three.js
       ↓
   Socket.IO
       ↓
NestJS Backend
       ↓
   PostgreSQL
       ↓
Docker Compose
```

The challenging part was not drawing the game. It was coordinating authentication, real-time events, multiplayer state, chat, persistence, and containerized services without letting the clients become the source of truth.

**Role:** Full-Stack Engineer.
**Status:** Archived — public repository, no live deployment.
**Focus:** Real-time systems, WebSockets, full-stack architecture, authentication, and containerization.

title: NoybStruct
description: A live software design-patterns learning platform, built with Next.js, TypeScript, Prisma, and PostgreSQL. Publicly accessible at struct.noybcore.com.
caseStudy:
A live software design-patterns learning platform. The site presents design patterns with structured explanations and code examples, providing a browsable reference for developers who want to move from concept to code without leaving the page.

The application is a full-stack **Next.js** project written in **TypeScript**, using **Prisma** as the ORM over **PostgreSQL** and **Auth.js** for session handling. The database schema is defined in Prisma and drives generated types that flow through to the application, so changes at the data layer surface as compile-time errors rather than runtime failures.

The interesting engineering work was in the data model rather than the UI: keeping pattern definitions, code samples, and per-user state in a schema that remains queryable as the pattern set grows. Prisma's type generation carries the schema through the stack and removes a class of integration bugs.

Live and publicly accessible.

**Role:** Full-Stack Engineer.
**Status:** Live.
**Focus:** Full-stack TypeScript, PostgreSQL schema design with Prisma, authentication, developer-facing content delivery.

title: API Developer Portal Template
description: A reusable, API-agnostic developer portal for building professional API documentation with data-driven content, API references, search, theming, and automated validation.
caseStudy:
A reusable developer portal foundation for publishing professional API documentation without coupling the frontend to a specific backend.

The project separates documentation content, site configuration, API reference data, navigation, branding, and application logic. This makes the portal adaptable to SaaS products, internal platforms, fintech APIs, logistics systems, and other HTTP APIs.

```text
Site Configuration
       ↓
Typed Documentation
       ↓
API Reference
       ↓
Search Index
       ↓
Developer Portal
```

The template provides responsive documentation navigation, client-side search, light/dark theming, reusable API reference components, typed content structures, and CI validation for linting, type checking, tests, and production builds.

**Role:** Frontend / Full-Stack Engineer.
**Status:** Live and public.
**Focus:** Developer experience, reusable frontend architecture, API documentation, and configuration-driven design.

title: Document Processing RAG Pipeline
description: Private backend project in active design and early implementation — asynchronous document processing, RAG architecture, and grounded retrieval.
caseStudy:
A private backend project exploring asynchronous document processing and retrieval-augmented generation. Currently in design and early implementation — not a deployed product.

The architecture is designed around an asynchronous pipeline where documents are stored, detected, parsed, cleaned, and prepared for retrieval without blocking the main application. The design uses **Temporal** for durable workflow orchestration, **Kafka** for asynchronous communication between processing stages, and **LangChain** for document processing and RAG. **LangGraph** is considered for the agentic workflow layer.

The diagram below shows the intended architecture. Parts of the pipeline are implemented; others remain design. The technologies listed reflect the design, not necessarily completed implementation.

```text
Document
   ↓
Storage
   ↓
File Detection
   ↓
Async Processing
   ├── Temporal
   ├── Kafka
   └── Document Parsing
   ↓
Text Extraction & Cleaning
   ↓
Chunking & Embeddings
   ↓
Vector Retrieval
   ↓
Grounded AI Response
```

**Role:** Backend Engineer — design and implementation.
**Status:** Private — design and active implementation. Not deployed.
**Focus:** Document-processing architecture, asynchronous workflow design, and RAG systems.

title: This Portfolio
description: A developer portfolio designed as a VS Code-inspired workspace, with configuration-driven projects, technical content, search, and a developer-focused interface.
caseStudy:
A personal developer portfolio built around the environment I actually use every day: the code editor.

The interface takes inspiration from VS Code with an explorer, tabs, status bar, command palette, terminal, and developer-oriented navigation. Project and content data are separated from the UI so new work can be added without modifying JSX components.

```text
src/data/
├── projects.json
├── blog.json
├── experience.json
├── who-i-am.json
└── site.json

        ↓

React UI
        ↓

Production Portfolio
```

The goal was not to reproduce an editor for the sake of novelty, but to create a portfolio that remains easy to maintain as the body of work grows.

**Role:** Software Engineer / Designer.
**Status:** Live and actively maintained.
**Focus:** Developer experience, configuration-driven UI, frontend architecture, and technical personal branding.

title: Dining Philosophers
description: A concurrency project exploring threads, mutexes, timing, deadlock prevention, and starvation through the classic Dining Philosophers problem.
caseStudy:
A concurrency exercise built around the classic Dining Philosophers problem.

The project focuses on coordinating multiple threads competing for shared resources while preventing deadlocks and minimizing starvation. Precise timing is critical because the simulation is defined by strict time-to-die, time-to-eat, and time-to-sleep constraints.

**Role:** Systems Programmer.
**Status:** Archived — public repository.
**Focus:** Threads, mutexes, synchronization, race conditions, and timing.

title: Docker Inception
description: A containerized WordPress infrastructure built from multiple Docker services, including Nginx, MariaDB, Redis, and supporting infrastructure.
caseStudy:
A containerized infrastructure project focused on understanding service isolation, networking, persistent storage, and multi-container orchestration.

The stack connects Nginx, WordPress, MariaDB, and Redis through Docker networking while separating responsibilities across services.

```text
          Nginx
            ↓
        WordPress
         ↙     ↘
    MariaDB    Redis
            
        Docker Network
```

**Role:** Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer.
**Status:** Archived — public repository.
**Focus:** Docker, service orchestration, networking, persistence, and infrastructure fundamentals.

title: STL from Scratch
description: A C++ implementation of core STL containers focused on templates, iterators, allocators, data structures, and container behavior.
caseStudy:
A 1337 systems project focused on understanding how standard C++ containers work internally by implementing their core behavior from scratch.

The project explores templates, iterators, memory management, allocators, tree-based structures, and container interfaces rather than relying on the standard library implementations.

**Role:** C++ / Systems Programmer.
**Status:** Archived — public repository.
**Focus:** Templates, data structures, memory management, iterators, and STL internals.

title: MiniShell
description: A Unix shell implemented in C with command parsing, pipes, redirections, environment variables, builtins, signals, and process management.
caseStudy:
A 1337 team project to build a functional Unix shell from scratch.

The implementation covers command parsing, environment variables, redirections, pipelines, builtin commands, process creation, and signal handling.

```text
Input
 ↓
Parser
 ↓
Command Structure
 ↓
Pipes / Redirections
 ↓
Processes
 ↓
Signals
```

**Role:** Systems Programmer.
**Status:** Archived — public repository.
**Focus:** Unix processes, file descriptors, pipes, signals, parsing, and shell behavior.

title: FT-WebServer
description: An HTTP server implemented in C++ with non-blocking I/O and epoll, designed to handle concurrent HTTP connections without relying on one thread per client.
caseStudy:
A low-level HTTP server written in C++ to understand how web servers handle sockets, HTTP requests, connections, and concurrent clients.

The project uses non-blocking sockets and **epoll** to manage multiple connections through an event-driven architecture rather than creating a dedicated thread for every client.

```text
Clients
  ↓
Sockets
  ↓
epoll
  ↓
Event Loop
  ↓
HTTP Parser
  ↓
Response
```

**Role:** Systems / Networking Engineer.
**Status:** Archived — public repository.
**Focus:** HTTP, sockets, event-driven I/O, epoll, concurrency, and networking fundamentals.
